messages:
Ava (Support): FYI we have a live customer (AcmeCorp) reporting OAuth login failures for both Google and GitHub SSO. They see an immediate browser error after redirect: "The redirect URI in the request, ... is not registered in the OAuth client." — they pasted screenshot.

Diego (SRE): Got it. error string looks like redirect_uri_mismatch on Google. Any chance they rotated redirect URL or use different hostname (www vs non-www)?

Ava (Support): Customer says nothing changed on their side, they do use our hosted login widget at https://app.acme.redwood.example.com/callback (VPC/private flow). They also mentioned PKCE in their app but not sure if configured.

Nina (Auth): Can we get their exact redirect_uri value from the browser? That usually nails it. Also want the full OAuth query params (state, code, code_verifier presence).

Ava (Support): Pasted from the browser console: 

```
GET /oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=redwood-client-123&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.acme.redwood.example.com%2Foauth%2Fcallback&scope=openid%20email&state=Zy12x&code_challenge=abcdef&code_challenge_method=S256
```

Ava (Support): The browser error when Google returns: 

```
Error: redirect_uri_mismatch
The redirect URI in the request, https://app.acme.redwood.example.com/oauth/callback, does not match the ones authorized for the OAuth client. Registered: https://app.acme.redwood.example.com/oauth/callback/
```

Sam (Eng): Looks like trailing slash mismatch on our redirect registered URI vs the one used in the request (notice one ends with /). Some identity providers are strict. But the other detail: they also reported GitHub giving a state mismatch on callback sometimes. Could be session sticky or multiple parallel flows.

Diego (SRE): Also saw reports where reverse proxies drop query params when doing a 302 -> rewriting host header. If the redirect URL is URL-encoded differently or missing trailing slash after proxy, provider will reject. Can we ask for a HAR or full network trace?

Ava (Support): Customer uploaded HAR and logs. HAR shows two authorize requests in quick succession (they retry automatically). Second request has a different state token. First auth flow gets a callback with code + state A, but app exchanges state B (the second). So server rejects: state mismatch. Error in our server logs: 

```
[2026-03-09T15:12:33Z] auth-service: warn state mismatch: got=eyJ... expected=eyJabc... session_id=abc-123 user_agent=Chrome/110
[2026-03-09T15:12:34Z] auth-service: info aborting token exchange invalid state
```

Nina (Auth): That matches classic double-submit. If the frontend triggers /authorize twice (race), the second state will overwrite server-side session state or the browser session only keeps the latest. PKCE: ensure code_verifier is tied to the matching state. Also make sure our callback handler looks at query state param before starting exchange.

Sam (Eng): Two remediation paths: (1) Make redirect URIs canonical (always register both with/without slash) and normalize incoming redirect_uri on the provider app config; (2) Harden our frontend to disable duplicate authorize clicks and to persist the first state in sessionStorage keyed by the login attempt id.

Ava (Support): Customer wants a step-by-step repro so they can test fix. Here's what I documented for them: 
1) Start a fresh browser session.
2) Trigger login, watch the first /authorize request (save its state parameter).
3) Quickly click login again (or reproduce flaky network to cause race).
4) Observe second /authorize with different state.
5) Observe callback contains code for first state, but app tries to exchange using second state -> state mismatch.

Diego (SRE): For immediate unblocking, ask them to update OAuth client redirect URIs in Google Cloud Console to include both variants (with and without trailing slash) and ensure GitHub app has exact match too. Also suggest they disable aggressive front-end retries.

Nina (Auth): Also verify PKCE handling: when the app generates code_challenge it must preserve the code_verifier server-side or in storage for the same ephemeral state. If the code_verifier is lost (or new one generated for second attempt), token exchange will return invalid_grant. Example exchange error we saw in logs: 

```
HTTP 400 from token endpoint: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"PKCE verification failed"}
```

Ava (Support): Customer reported an extra issue: after fixing redirect, they still get intermittent 400s for token exchange with GitHub: 

```
{"error":"bad_verification_code","error_description":"The code passed is incorrect or expired."}
```

Sam (Eng): That can be expiration + race. GitHub codes are single-use and short-lived. If two parallel authorize flows are inflight and one code is consumed, the other will fail. We should recommend single-flight logic.

Ava (Support): Action items so we can reply to customer: 
- Nina: confirm server-side session handling and whether we overwrite state on concurrent requests.
- Sam: quick patch suggestion for frontend to gate duplicate authorize clicks and persist state in sessionStorage. Could you paste a small snippet?
- Diego: sanity check proxy rewrite rules for trailing slash and query-preserving 302s.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: auth-service v2.14.1 -> canary

Nina (Auth): From auth-service code: we currently store state in an in-memory map keyed by session cookie and we do a straight replace: store[stateKey] = newState. That overwrites on second request. I'll change to store a list of recent states (LIFO) and validate against any recent match (window 30s) to tolerate quick retried flows. Planning small PR.

Sam (Eng): Frontend snippet for gating: 

```
// in login.js
if (window.__login_in_progress) return;
window.__login_in_progress = true;
// generate state + code_verifier, save to sessionStorage
sessionStorage.setItem('oauth_state', state);
window.location = authorizeUrl;
```

Add a cleanup on callback success/failure to clear the flag.

Diego (SRE): I'll look into proxy rules. Quick workaround for customer: register both redirect URIs (with/without trailing slash) and make sure the exact host + path used by client is present in the provider app. That usually unblocks Google/GitHub immediately.

Ava (Support): Great. I'll reply with repro steps, the temporary workaround (register both URIs), and ETA of the auth-service fix (Nina please add ETA). Also will suggest frontend gating. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Nina (Auth): PR open: https://git.internal/redwood/auth-service/pull/492 - small change to accept previous state tokens within 30s window. ETA review + canary: 2 hours.

Ava (Support): Posting final message to customer with steps and links. Closing thread when customer confirms.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy successful: auth-service v2.14.1 -> canary -> 3 nodes

Sam (Eng): Follow-up note: consider adding server-side dedupe token (login_attempt_id) returned to frontend so we don't rely solely on state string for matching across retries. Saves us from these edge races.
